newsitem.title: NIGER: President's supporters win last three Niger seats.
newsitem.headline: President's supporters win last three Niger seats.

text.p: Supporters of President Ibrahim Bare Mainassara won the last three seats in Niger's national assembly in weekend elections, provisional results from the independent national election commission showed on Monday.
Members of the Union of Independents for Democratic Renewal (UNIRD) won the three undecided seats in the 83-seat parliament after Sunday by-elections in Aguie and Mirriah constituencies.
UNIRD now holds 59 of the 83 seats in the assembly which was formally installed on December 20.
The West African nation's supreme court ordered the reruns after a November 23 parliamentary election, citing fraud.
An eight-party opposition alliance boycotted the November poll accusing Mainassara of rigging a July presidential poll to legitimise his rule after a January 1996 coup.
Opposition supporters, many of them women, staged weekend protests demanding the release of detained party militants.
Three opposition leaders, including former president Mahamane Ousmane, the man Mainassara toppled, are being held and investigated on charges of threatening state security.
They were among more than 60 people detained after police broke up banned opposition protests on January 11 to demand greater access to state media.
Former colonial power France and the United States, which has condemned Mainassara's election as fraudulent, have urged the release of the three opposition leaders.
Sunday's voter turnout was 31.79 percent after 39.17 percent in November.
